title: Sara Duterte decries dad Rodrigo's required attendance in ICC trial
summary: Vice President Sara Duterte on Friday said it was "unfair" that her father, former president Rodrigo Duterte, is being required to attend trial proceedings for his crimes against humanity case before…

blocks.text: Vice President Sara Duterte on Friday said it was "unfair" that her father, former president Rodrigo Duterte, is being required to attend trial proceedings for his crimes against humanity case before the International Criminal Court (ICC) on a daily basis.
Speaking before the media, the vice president stressed that her father is already 81 years old and is unlikely to focus throughout an eight-hour trial.
"I think it's unfair that they are demanding that he attends the trial every day as long as there is a trial, because of his age. Clearly, he cannot sit eight hours a day on a chair," she said.
"And I don't think he can focus and give his time and attention, particularly his attention, to something for eight hours. So I think it's unfair to demand that of an 81-year-old man," she added.
The vice president expressed hope that the court would allow her father to attend the trial virtually.
"Unfortunately, that was not given him, so I hope that his defense team will ask for that in the coming days," she said.
The ICC Chamber III earlier found the elder Duterte fit to stand trial, stating that he "is able to effectively exercise his fair trial rights in the proceedings."
The court chamber also ordered measures to facilitate Duterte's participation in the proceedings.
The trial is scheduled to open on November 30, 2026.
However, Sara Duterte stood firm that she is not expecting a fair trial from the ICC.

"Particularly because this is the only remaining case in the ICC already. And I think the ICC, after the ganging up of superpowers, they would want to make a statement that they are in the right," she said.
"So there is no one else there that they would like to make a statement to, and that's the case of Rodrigo Duterte," she added.
Trial aside, the vice president said she and her family have no complaints as to how the ICC is treating Rodrigo in the detention unit.
She said the Scheveningen Prison in The Hague, Netherlands has been "taking good care" of the former president. — VDV, GMA News
